paragraph.heading: Indian tribe.—
paragraph.content: The term “Indian tribe” has the meaning given the term in section 4 of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 5304).

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of Agriculture.

paragraph.heading: State.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “State” means—

subparagraph.content: a State;
the District of Columbia;
the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico; and
any other territory or possession of the United States.

paragraph.heading: State department of agriculture.—
paragraph.content: The term “State department of agriculture” means the agency, commission, or department of a State government responsible for agriculture in the State.

paragraph.heading: Tribal government.—
paragraph.content: The term “Tribal government” means the governing body of an Indian tribe.

subtitle.editorialNote: [Note: Effective on November 12, 2026, section 781 of division B of Public Law 119–37 provides for amendments to section 297A. Upon such date, section 297A reads as follows:]

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The term “hemp” means the plant Cannabis sativa L. and any part of that plant, including the seeds thereof and all derivatives, extracts, cannabinoids, isomers, acids, salts, and salts of isomers, whether growing or not, with a total tetrahydrocannabinols concentration (including tetrahydrocannabinolic acid) of not more than 0.3 percent on a dry weight basis.

subparagraph.heading: Inclusion.—
subparagraph.content: Such term includes industrial hemp.

subparagraph.heading: Exclusions.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Such term does not include—

clause.content: any viable seeds from a Cannabis sativa L. plant that exceeds a total tetrahydrocannabinols concentration (including tetrahydrocannabinolic acid) of 0.3 percent in the plant on a dry weight basis; or

clause.chapeau: any intermediate hemp-derived cannabinoid products containing—

subclause.content: cannabinoids that are not capable of being naturally produced by a Cannabis sativa L. plant;

item.content: are capable of being naturally produced by a Cannabis sativa L. plant; and
were synthesized or manufactured outside the plant; or

subclause.chapeau: more than 0.3 percent combined total of—

item.content: any other cannabinoids that have similar effects (or are marketed to have similar effects) on humans or animals as a tetrahydrocannabinol (as determined by the Secretary of Health and Human Services); or

clause.content: any intermediate hemp-derived cannabinoid products which are marketed or sold as a final product or directly to an end consumer for personal or household use; or

clause.chapeau: any final hemp-derived cannabinoid products containing—

subclause.content: cannabinoids that are not capable of being naturally produced by a Cannabis sativa L. plant;

item.content: are capable of being naturally produced by a Cannabis sativa L. plant; and
were synthesized or manufactured outside the plant; or

subclause.chapeau: greater than 0.4 milligrams combined total per container of—

item.content: any other cannabinoids that have similar effects (or are marketed to have similar effects) on humans or animals as a tetrahydrocannabinol (as determined by the Secretary of Health and Human Services).

paragraph.heading: Industrial hemp.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “industrial hemp” means hemp—

subparagraph.content: grown for the use of the stalk of the plant, fiber produced from such a stalk, or any other non-cannabinoid derivative, mixture, preparation, or manufacture of such a stalk;
grown for the use of the whole grain, oil, cake, nut, hull, or any other non-cannabinoid compound, derivative, mixture, preparation, or manufacture of the seeds of such plant;

grown for purposes of producing microgreens or other edible hemp leaf products intended for human consumption that are derived from an immature hemp plant that is grown from seeds that do not exceed the threshold for total tetrahydrocannabinols concentration specified in paragraph (1)(C)(i);

that is a plant that does not enter the stream of commerce and is intended to support hemp research at an institution of higher education (as defined in section 101 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 1001)) or an independent research institute; or
grown for the use of a viable seed of the plant produced solely for the production or manufacture of any material described in subparagraphs (A) through (D).

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The term “hemp-derived cannabinoid product” means any intermediate or final product derived from hemp (other than industrial hemp), that—

clause.content: contains cannabinoids in any form; and
is intended for human or animal use through any means of application or administration, such as inhalation, ingestion, or topical application.

subparagraph.chapeau: The term “intermediate hemp-derived cannabinoid product” means a hemp-derived cannabinoid product which—

clause.content: is not yet in the final form or preparation marketed or intended to be used or consumed by a human or animal; or

is a powder, liquid, tablet, oil, or other product form which is intended or marketed to be mixed, dissolved, formulated, or otherwise added to or prepared with or into any other substance prior to administration or consumption.

subparagraph.content: The term “container” means the innermost wrapping, packaging, or vessel in direct contact with a final hemp-derived cannabinoid product in which the final hemp-derived cannabinoid product is enclosed for retail sale to consumers, such as a jar, bottle, bag, box, packet, can, carton, or cartridge.
The term container excludes bulk shipping containers or outer wrappings that are not essential for the final retail delivery or sale to an end consumer for personal or household use.

subparagraph.heading: Exclusion.—
subparagraph.content: Such term does not include a drug that is the subject of an application approved under subsection (c) or (j) of section 505 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 355).

paragraph.heading: Indian tribe.—
paragraph.content: The term “Indian tribe” has the meaning given the term in section 4 of the Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act (25 U.S.C. 5304).

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of Agriculture.

paragraph.heading: State.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “State” means—

subparagraph.content: a State;
the District of Columbia;
the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico; and
any other territory or possession of the United States.

paragraph.heading: State department of agriculture.—
paragraph.content: The term “State department of agriculture” means the agency, commission, or department of a State government responsible for agriculture in the State.

paragraph.heading: Tribal government.—
paragraph.content: The term “Tribal government” means the governing body of an Indian tribe.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: A State or Indian tribe desiring to have primary regulatory authority over the production of hemp in the State or territory of the Indian tribe shall submit to the Secretary, through the State department of agriculture (in consultation with the Governor and chief law enforcement officer of the State) or the Tribal government, as applicable, a plan under which the State or Indian tribe monitors and regulates that production as described in paragraph (2).

paragraph.heading: Contents.—
paragraph.chapeau: A State or Tribal plan referred to in paragraph (1)—

subparagraph.chapeau: shall only be required to include—

clause.content: a practice to maintain relevant information regarding land on which hemp is produced in the State or territory of the Indian tribe, including a legal description of the land, for a period of not less than 3 calendar years;

a procedure for testing, using post-decarboxylation or other similarly reliable methods, delta-9 tetrahydrocannabinol concentration levels of hemp produced in the State or territory of the Indian tribe;

clause.chapeau: a procedure for the effective disposal of—

subclause.content: plants, whether growing or not, that are produced in violation of this subtitle; and
products derived from those plants;

clause.content: a procedure to comply with the enforcement procedures under subsection (e);
a procedure for conducting annual inspections of, at a minimum, a random sample of hemp producers to verify that hemp is not produced in violation of this subtitle;
a procedure for submitting the information described in section 297C(d)(2), as applicable, to the Secretary not more than 30 days after the date on which the information is received; and
a certification that the State or Indian tribe has the resources and personnel to carry out the practices and procedures described in clauses (i) through (vi); and

subparagraph.content: may include any other practice or procedure established by a State or Indian tribe, as applicable, to the extent that the practice or procedure is consistent with this subtitle.

paragraph.heading: Relation to state and tribal law.—

subparagraph.heading: No preemption.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Nothing in this subsection preempts or limits any law of a State or Indian tribe that—

clause.content: regulates the production of hemp; and
is more stringent than this subtitle.

subparagraph.heading: References in plans.—
subparagraph.content: A State or Tribal plan referred to in paragraph (1) may include a reference to a law of the State or Indian tribe regulating the production of hemp, to the extent that law is consistent with this subtitle.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than 60 days after receipt of a State or Tribal plan under subsection (a), the Secretary shall—

subparagraph.content: approve the State or Tribal plan if the State or Tribal plan complies with subsection (a); or
disapprove the State or Tribal plan only if the State or Tribal plan does not comply with subsection (a).

paragraph.heading: Amended plans.—
paragraph.content: If the Secretary disapproves a State or Tribal plan under paragraph (1)(B), the State, through the State department of agriculture (in consultation with the Governor and chief law enforcement officer of the State) or the Tribal government, as applicable, may submit to the Secretary an amended State or Tribal plan that complies with subsection (a).

paragraph.heading: Consultation.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall consult with the Attorney General in carrying out this subsection.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may conduct an audit of the compliance of a State or Indian tribe with a State or Tribal plan approved under subsection (b).

paragraph.heading: Noncompliance.—
paragraph.chapeau: If the Secretary determines under an audit conducted under paragraph (1) that a State or Indian tribe is not materially in compliance with a State or Tribal plan—

subparagraph.content: the Secretary shall collaborate with the State or Indian tribe to develop a corrective action plan in the case of a first instance of noncompliance; and
the Secretary may revoke approval of the State or Tribal plan in the case of a second or subsequent instance of noncompliance.

subsection.heading: Technical Assistance.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may provide technical assistance to a State or Indian tribe in the development of a State or Tribal plan under subsection (a).

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: A violation of a State or Tribal plan approved under subsection (b) shall be subject to enforcement solely in accordance with this subsection.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: A hemp producer in a State or the territory of an Indian tribe for which a State or Tribal plan is approved under subsection (b) shall be subject to subparagraph (B) of this paragraph if the State department of agriculture or Tribal government, as applicable, determines that the hemp producer has negligently violated the State or Tribal plan, including by negligently—

clause.content: failing to provide a legal description of land on which the producer produces hemp;
failing to obtain a license or other required authorization from the State department of agriculture or Tribal government, as applicable; or
producing Cannabis sativa L. with a delta-9 tetrahydrocannabinol concentration of more than 0.3 percent on a dry weight basis.

subparagraph.heading: Corrective action plan.—
subparagraph.chapeau: A hemp producer described in subparagraph (A) shall comply with a plan established by the State department of agriculture or Tribal government, as applicable, to correct the negligent violation, including—

clause.content: a reasonable date by which the hemp producer shall correct the negligent violation; and

a requirement that the hemp producer shall periodically report to the State department of agriculture or Tribal government, as applicable, on the compliance of the hemp producer with the State or Tribal plan for a period of not less than the next 2 calendar years.

subparagraph.heading: Result of negligent violation.—
subparagraph.content: A hemp producer that negligently violates a State or Tribal plan under subparagraph (A) shall not as a result of that violation be subject to any criminal enforcement action by the Federal Government or any State government, Tribal government, or local government.

subparagraph.heading: Repeat violations.—
subparagraph.content: A hemp producer that negligently violates a State or Tribal plan under subparagraph (A) 3 times in a 5-year period shall be ineligible to produce hemp for a period of 5 years beginning on the date of the third violation.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: If the State department of agriculture or Tribal government in a State or the territory of an Indian tribe for which a State or Tribal plan is approved under subsection (b), as applicable, determines that a hemp producer in the State or territory has violated the State or Tribal plan with a culpable mental state greater than negligence—

clause.chapeau: the State department of agriculture or Tribal government, as applicable, shall immediately report the hemp producer to—

subclause.content: the Attorney General; and
the chief law enforcement officer of the State or Indian tribe, as applicable; and

clause.content: paragraph (1) of this subsection shall not apply to the violation.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.chapeau: Except as provided in clause (ii), any person convicted of a felony relating to a controlled substance under State or Federal law before, on, or after the date of enactment of this subtitle shall be ineligible, during the 10-year period following the date of the conviction—

subclause.content: to participate in the program established under this section or section 297C; and
to produce hemp under any regulations or guidelines issued under section 297D(a).

clause.heading: Exception.—
clause.content: Clause (i) shall not apply to any person growing hemp lawfully with a license, registration, or authorization under a pilot program authorized by section 7606 of the Agricultural Act of 2014 (7 U.S.C. 5940) before the date of enactment of this subtitle.

subparagraph.heading: False statement.—
subparagraph.content: Any person who materially falsifies any information contained in an application to participate in the program established under this section shall be ineligible to participate in that program.

subsection.heading: Effect.—
subsection.chapeau: Nothing in this section prohibits the production of hemp in a State or the territory of an Indian tribe—

paragraph.content: for which a State or Tribal plan is not approved under this section, if the production of hemp is in accordance with section 297C or other Federal laws (including regulations); and
if the production of hemp is not otherwise prohibited by the State or Indian tribe.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: In the case of a State or Indian tribe for which a State or Tribal plan is not approved under section 297B, the production of hemp in that State or the territory of that Indian tribe shall be subject to a plan established by the Secretary to monitor and regulate that production in accordance with paragraph (2).

paragraph.heading: Content.—
paragraph.chapeau: A plan established by the Secretary under paragraph (1) shall include—

subparagraph.content: a practice to maintain relevant information regarding land on which hemp is produced in the State or territory of the Indian tribe, including a legal description of the land, for a period of not less than 3 calendar years;

a procedure for testing, using post-decarboxylation or other similarly reliable methods, delta-9 tetrahydrocannabinol concentration levels of hemp produced in the State or territory of the Indian tribe;

subparagraph.chapeau: a procedure for the effective disposal of—

clause.content: plants, whether growing or not, that are produced in violation of this subtitle; and
products derived from those plants;

subparagraph.content: a procedure to comply with the enforcement procedures under subsection (c)(2);
a procedure for conducting annual inspections of, at a minimum, a random sample of hemp producers to verify that hemp is not produced in violation of this subtitle; and
such other practices or procedures as the Secretary considers to be appropriate, to the extent that the practice or procedure is consistent with this subtitle.

subsection.heading: Licensing.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall establish a procedure to issue licenses to hemp producers in accordance with a plan established under subsection (a).

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: In the case of a State or Indian tribe for which a State or Tribal plan is not approved under section 297B, it shall be unlawful to produce hemp in that State or the territory of that Indian tribe without a license issued by the Secretary under subsection (b).

paragraph.heading: Negligent and other violations.—
paragraph.content: A violation of a plan established under subsection (a) shall be subject to enforcement in accordance with paragraphs (2) and (3) of section 297B(e), except that the Secretary shall carry out that enforcement instead of a State department of agriculture or Tribal government.

paragraph.heading: Reporting to attorney general.—
paragraph.content: In the case of a State or Indian tribe covered by paragraph (1), the Secretary shall report the production of hemp without a license issued by the Secretary under subsection (b) to the Attorney General.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall—

subparagraph.content: collect the information described in paragraph (2); and
make the information collected under subparagraph (A) accessible in real time to Federal, State, territorial, and local law enforcement.

paragraph.heading: Content.—
paragraph.chapeau: The information collected by the Secretary under paragraph (1) shall include—

subparagraph.chapeau: contact information for each hemp producer in a State or the territory of an Indian tribe for which—

clause.content: a State or Tribal plan is approved under section 297B(b); or
a plan is established by the Secretary under this section;

subparagraph.content: a legal description of the land on which hemp is grown by each hemp producer described in subparagraph (A); and

subparagraph.chapeau: for each hemp producer described in subparagraph (A)—

subclause.content: a license or other required authorization from the State department of agriculture or Tribal government, as applicable; or
a license from the Secretary; and

clause.content: any changes to the status.

section.heading: REGULATIONS AND GUIDELINES; EFFECT ON OTHER LAW.

subsection.heading: Promulgation of Regulations and Guidelines; Report.—

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall promulgate regulations and guidelines to implement this subtitle as expeditiously as practicable.

subparagraph.heading: Consultation with attorney general.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall consult with the Attorney General on the promulgation of regulations and guidelines under subparagraph (A).

paragraph.heading: Report.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall annually submit to the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate a report containing updates on the implementation of this subtitle.

subsection.heading: Authority.—
subsection.content: Subject to subsection (c)(3)(B), the Secretary shall have sole authority to promulgate Federal regulations and guidelines that relate to the production of hemp, including Federal regulations and guidelines that relate to the implementation of sections 297B and 297C.

subsection.heading: Effect on Other Law.—
subsection.chapeau: Nothing in this subtitle shall affect or modify—

paragraph.content: the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 301 et seq.);
section 351 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 262); or

paragraph.chapeau: the authority of the Commissioner of Food and Drugs and the Secretary of Health and Human Services—

subparagraph.chapeau: under—

clause.content: the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 301 et seq.); or
section 351 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 262); or

subparagraph.content: to promulgate Federal regulations and guidelines that relate to the production of hemp under the Act described in subparagraph (A)(i) or the section described in subparagraph (A)(ii).

section.heading: AUTHORIZATION OF APPROPRIATIONS.
section.content: There are authorized to be appropriated such sums as are necessary to carry out this subtitle.
